name: Seaglass
description: Refers to the subjective cognitive state of someone whose augmentations are mismatched, outdated, or incompatible with current system standards — functioning, technically, but with a quality of smoothed-down wrongness, like sea glass: once sharp, now blunted by time and friction into something pretty but no longer what it was. Used to describe both the aug-user's experience and, more critically, how they appear to others — slightly delayed, slightly off, beautiful in a broken way. Common among Shelf residents running decade-old chrome.
cultural_impact: The term has developed an unexpected secondary life in art and aesthetics — 'seaglass' as a visual style celebrates the degraded-beautiful quality of old chrome and mismatched augmentation. Several Shelf art collectives have built entire aesthetic movements around seaglass aesthetics, which has predictably attracted Tier 3-4 appropriation.
key_figures: Augusto 'Gus' Ferrara-Wondimu (Shelf aug-tech, known for keeping old chrome running)
locations: The Littoral Collective studio space, reclaimed warehouse district
story_hooks: A Tier 1 resident running 20-year-old chrome starts experiencing seaglass states that feel less like degradation and more like clarity — as if the old system is accessing something the new ones can't. Someone in a corponation's R&D division finds out and wants to know why.

The Littoral Collective's seaglass aesthetic show gets picked up by a Tier 4 gallery, and the original artists must decide whether to participate in the sanitized version or sabotage it — while one of their members is tempted by the money.
A fixer needs someone who runs seaglass — because only degraded, non-standard chrome can slip through a corponation's biometric security net undetected.
definition: The state of running mismatched or outdated augmentations — functional but with a smoothed-down, slightly-off quality. As an aesthetic: the beauty of old chrome and degraded tech. As an insult (rare): calling someone a relic. As a compliment: calling someone weathered into something worth looking at.
usage_example: 'She's running seaglass on everything below her collarbone — you can see the lag in her eyes, but honestly, she's the most interesting person in the room.'
spread: Strong in Tier 1-2; aesthetic version being adopted by Tier 3 art scenes; term itself beginning to appear in Tier 3 casual speech.
